notes: Fix: I removed the port-specific GND, VCC and A1-A4 edges between mkr1 and shield1. On the shield those ports are screw terminals, which can't join to the MKR board's header pins. The MKR board plugs into the shield's female headers, which the catalogue card doesn't list as ports. So the stack is one port-less 'joined' edge, mkr1 to shield1.
The 5 V vs 3.3 V warning came from the VCC edge I removed. Nothing now puts 5 V on the shield's 3.3 V-rated VCC. The MKR board runs at 3.3 V logic, and the shield's low-power side is 3.3 V.
The tutorial says any MKR family board; I used the MKR WiFi 1010 (arduino-mkr1000-wifi).
The relays are wired inside the shield to MKR pins 1 and 2, so there are no wires for them.

The circuit image was not available, so the LED wiring is my assumption. Pin 3 goes through a jumper wire to LED_1's anode. Its cathode goes through a 220 ohm resistor to the breadboard ground rail. Pin 4 does the same for LED_2. One jumper wire takes MKR GND to the ground rail.
Resistor value (220 ohm) and LED colours are assumed, as the tutorial doesn't give them.
The 24V supply and 24V lamp on the high-power terminals are only an illustrative example, so I did not build them.
